trigger: page.json, index page, page-level, rename page, html_header, page css
rule: Index page.json is un-editable via Buildprint — Any edit to the index page's page.
fix: Any edit to the index page's page.json — even one character — trips a pre-existing blocking check error (canvas-root-name-validity: 'index' is a reserved name). Never rename index (required to run the app) and never plan page-level edits on it; page-scoped changes need another mechanism (e.g. per-element states or a reusable).
errorSig: you can't name a page 'index' because it is a reserved name

trigger: light mode, dark mode, theming, theme, bptheme, dark_theme
rule: CRS light-mode pattern: bptheme element states — Theming is per-element conditional states keyed on Current User's dark_theme is_false, overriding colors with the paired '· Light' tokens from tokens.
fix: Theming is per-element conditional states keyed on Current User's dark_theme is_false, overriding colors with the paired '· Light' tokens from tokens.json (e.g. BG Secondary ↔ BG Secondary · Light). Copy the pattern from existing elements (e.g. Toast); never edit shared style files for one page — that leaks to every page using the style.

trigger: scratch, .context, workspace root, check flags, analysis files
rule: No scratch files inside the Bubble worktree — buildprint check flags any non-schema directory (e.
fix: buildprint check flags any non-schema directory (e.g. .context/) at the workspace root as an invalid entry. Write scratch/analysis files OUTSIDE the worktree; rm -rf is guard-blocked, so stray files must be deleted individually before check passes.

trigger: git checkout, git reset, revert, restore file, discard changes
rule: Reverting uncommitted worktree edits — git checkout/reset are blocked by the safety gate in BP sessions.
fix: git checkout/reset are blocked by the safety gate in BP sessions. To revert an uncommitted file, Read the synced content and Edit it back manually — or ask Vlad for a one-off approval. Do not retry the blocked git command.

trigger: python, python3, local script, aggregation script
rule: Use node, not python, for local scripts — python/python3 are not installed on the Windows host — local aggregation/analysis scripts in BP sessions must be written for node (which is always available).

rule: When buildprint sync fails with Unauthorized, don't assume stale data — check sync status first; if workspace matches latest snapshot, the error is transient auth, not staleness.
fix: Run `buildprint sync status` to confirm workspace version matches latest snapshot; if it does, proceed — the Unauthorized is a transient token hiccup, not data staleness.

rule: buildprint utils generate-ids uses positional count argument, not the --count named flag.
fix: Use `buildprint utils generate-ids <count>` (e.g., `buildprint utils generate-ids 4`), not `--count`.

trigger: shell loops, shell scripts, bash execution in sandbox
rule: Sandbox blocks shell scripts with certain syntax patterns (simple_expansion, conditionals) — use Node or HTML/JS artifacts instead.
fix: Use `node <script.js>` for local scripts or create an HTML artifact with embedded JavaScript for browser-based output.

trigger: testing buildprint connection, checking buildprint status, troubleshooting buildprint
rule: buildprint has no 'status' command; use 'buildprint project list' or 'buildprint link' to test connection.
fix: Run `buildprint project list` to diagnose connectivity; it will either succeed or fail with the actual error (e.g., token revoked).

trigger: buildprint CLI token revoked, token invalid, buildprint project list fails, buildprint link fails
rule: When buildprint CLI returns 'token is invalid or has been revoked', the token cannot be refreshed via CLI — it must be regenerated in the Buildprint UI.
fix: Generate a new token at Buildprint Agent → Integrations → CLI, then run `buildprint link <new-token>` to reconnect.
errorSig: could not link buildprint cli token is invalid or has been revoked

trigger: MCP connectors, external service integrations, Gmail, Google Workspace, first use of permission-gated MCP tools
rule: MCP connectors for external services (Gmail, Google Drive, etc.) require explicit permission grant from the user's Claude interface before the tool can execute — the assistant cannot proceed and must request user approval.
fix: When a tool call returns permission denied, look for a permission dialog in your Claude interface and click Allow (or Always Allow). If no prompt appears, check whether your client has permissions auto-denied in settings. After approval, retry the operation.
errorSig: requested permissions to use mcp claude ai but you haven't granted it yet

rule: Connecting an OAuth service (e.g., Gmail) and granting per-tool permissions in Claude Code are two separate configuration gates; one does not automatically enable the other.
fix: After OAuth connection, explicitly grant tool permissions via Claude Code settings or by responding to tool-permission prompts when a tool-use attempt surfaces them. Retry the tool call after granting.
errorSig: mcp service tool you haven't granted it yet

trigger: MCP tool permission prompts, Claude Code UI
rule: Permission dialogs for MCP tools may surface as out-of-band UI elements (banners, notifications, pending-action buttons) rather than inline chat messages, depending on the client.
fix: After a tool call fails with a permission error, check for permission dialogs outside the chat window (notification center, pending-actions area, settings panel) in addition to in-chat messages, then retry.

trigger: MCP connectors, Gmail authorization, Toolsearch gmail queries
rule: When Gmail MCP connector OAuth succeeds but API calls fail with 'insufficient authentication scopes', the Gmail permission checkbox was not approved during the Google OAuth consent screen.
fix: Disconnect the Gmail connector (MCP settings), reconnect it, and on the Google OAuth screen explicitly approve the Gmail read permission checkbox alongside Calendar/Drive permissions.
